description: What the organization measures about itself, and what it deliberately does not claim to measure. The purpose is to answer whether this way of working is better than the alternative, which is a question no amount of architecture answers on its own.
why: An engineering organization that cannot say whether it is improving is a set of opinions. The point of a durable record is that these numbers are derivable from it rather than estimated.
Every metric here is computed from what the work items already record. Nothing is instrumented specially, because a measurement that needs its own bookkeeping is one that stops being kept.

the_metric_that_matters.name: human intervention rate
the_metric_that_matters.means: How many times a human had to act, per unit of work, for it to progress.
the_metric_that_matters.why: The goal is not zero. A system that never asks a human has either solved engineering or stopped noticing when it should ask, and the second is far more likely. What the number is for is the trend: whether autonomy is increasing while the gates that matter stay in place.
counts_as_intervention: an approval recorded against a work item
an escalation that reached the human owner
an open decision the organization refused to guess
a replan, because it means the plan a human accepted was wrong
does_not_count: an agent verdict, which is the organization reviewing itself
an escalation that a lead or head resolved without a human
a guard denial, which is the system working rather than a person intervening

throughput.name: cycle time from open to accepted

enforcement.name: completions blocked by a failing definition of done

not_measured.token_cost: SubagentStop carries no usage figures. The task-notification block does, and nothing parses it. Reporting an estimate here would be a number people would plan against.
not_measured.wall_clock_per_task: Recorded only as started_at and last_activity, which measure elapsed time rather than work done. A task that sat overnight and one that ran for eight hours look identical.
not_measured.defect_escape_rate: Requires knowing which production defects trace to which change. The link exists in the artifact model and nothing populates it yet.
not_measured.agent_utilisation: Would need a spawn count per role over time. The audit log has the events; nothing aggregates them.
not_measured.human_approvals: Recorded on artifacts, not on the work item, and nothing writes an approvals field there. It was being summed into the human intervention rate as a structural zero, which made the rate look better the more it was trusted.
not_measured.open_decisions: Same: the work item has no decisions field and no writer for one. A DEC artifact is where an open decision lives.
not_measured.review_rejection_rate: A reviewer's verdict lives on the artifact header, which the work item store does not read. Listed under quality below as an intention, not a number this produces.
not_measured.stages_skipped: The graph records the stages it planned, not the ones the organization chose not to plan, so there is nothing to count against.

honesty_rule: A metric that cannot be computed from the durable record is listed under not_measured with the reason, never estimated. An organization that reports a number it cannot derive teaches its own people not to trust the rest.
why_keys: Every measured entry names the identifier the tool must produce, so validate_plugin can check that the policy and the code agree in both directions. The check used to read the policy's existence and not its contents.
